title: Scalable and customizable parallel flow-through reactors for microbial mats
author: Vanzin, Peel, et al.

steps.title: Install Flow-Through Reactor Drain
steps.instruction: Install a gravity-driven effluent port into the metal planter.

substeps.instruction: Mark the bottom of the planter to drill in the center and 3 cm from the end.
Use a center punch to indent, then drill a 1/2" (1.25 cm) hole using a drill press or hand drill; remove sharp edges with a deburring tool.
Prepare a Swagelok 1/4" (0.635 cm) stainless steel bulkhead unit by rolling a 1/2 in. (1.25 cm) rubber gasket onto it and attaching plumber's putty of similar size underneath.
Slide the bulkhead union into the hole with the gasket and putty on the interior bottom; tighten the nut from underneath and remove excess putty.
If a higher water column is needed, cut stainless steel tubing to size using a hack saw/vice or vertical band saw, and smooth the cut with a file.
Attach the stainless steel tube using the provided ferrule set and compression nuts.
Fill the container with water and monitor for leaks for at least one hour.

steps.title: Set Up Influent Lines
steps.instruction: Connect the influent delivery system to the reactor.

substeps.instruction: Attach influent lines using a plexiglass holder with drilled holes at the inlet.
Use tape to secure tubing above the water column to prevent contamination.

steps.title: Assemble Mobile Cart and Frame
steps.instruction: Prepare the support structure for the reactors and lighting.

substeps.instruction: Assemble the mobile cart per manufacturer instructions.
Drill 3/4 in. (1.9 cm) holes for drains on the top shelf, spaced evenly based on the number of reactors (e.g., four reactors on a 36 in. x 24 in. cart).
Optional: Install furniture leveling pads under planters for leveling.
Build a frame (approx. 0.6 m width, 0.9 m length, 0.6 m height) using zinc-plated steel angle posts, wood, T-slot rails, or plastic.
Optional: Attach a plexiglass shelf to the top of the frame for storage of probes and meters.

steps.title: Install Lighting System
steps.instruction: Set up dimmable LED grow lights to simulate diel cycling.

substeps.instruction: Install full-spectrum LED growing lights according to manufacturer instructions.
Cut the cord below the dimmer switch, strip wires, and attach them to a 0-10 V dimming controller.
Attach the light to the frame using provided hangers, ensuring the lights are 0.5 m (18") above the water surface.
Optional: Secure the dimmer controller to the frame or cart using zip ties or bolts.

steps.title: Configure Pump and Tubing
steps.instruction: Install the peristaltic pump and sterile tubing.

substeps.instruction: Autoclave tubing prior to use and replace weekly to prevent biofouling.
Install 2-stop tubing into the Ismatec pump cassettes.
Connect influent source to reactors, using heavy blunt end Luer-lok needles with male tubing connectors to weigh the tubing to the bottom of the influent bucket.
Secure the pump to the cart handles with utility cords or straps (or place on frame/under cart if larger).
Calibrate the pump flow rate using the bucket and stopwatch method (recording mass of liquid over set time) to create a linear regression for pump settings.

steps.title: Prepare Silica Stock Solution
steps.instruction: Create a 1 mM sodium metasilicate pentahydrate stock.

substeps.instruction: Measure 0.2260 g Na2SiO3•5H2O into 1 L of Milli-Q® water.
Store in a 1 L media bottle at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare Metals Stock Solution
steps.instruction: Create a concentrated trace metals stock.

substeps.instruction: Measure the following into 1 L of Milli-Q® water: disodium EDTA (5.20 g), FeCl2•4H2O (1.50 g), CoCl2•6H2O (0.19 g), MnCl2•4H2O (0.10 g), ZnCl2 (0.07 g), H3BO3 (0.06 g), NaMoO4•2H2O (0.04 g), CuCl2•2H2O (0.02 g), and NiCl2•6H2O (0.02 g).
Filter the stock from a 1 L volumetric flask into an autoclaved, dark (taped/foiled) 1 L media bottle containing an autoclaved stir bar.
Store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Influent Growth Media
steps.instruction: Prepare 20 L batches of synthetic river water in 5-gallon buckets.

substeps.instruction: Determine a 20 L fill line in a 5-gallon bucket using a graduated cylinder, then empty the bucket.
Clean the bucket and lid: scrub with diluted Alconox, rinse with tap water (3x), rinse with dilute bleach, and rinse with DI water (3x).
Fill the bucket approximately 1/2 to 3/4 full with DI water.
Pipette 1 mL of Silica stock and 20 mL of Metals stock into the container.
Add the following salts: MgSO4•7H2O (2.46 g), CaCl2 (4.7 g), K2HPO4 (0.19 g), NaHCO3 (6.05 g), Na2SO4 (0.99 g), KCl (0.49 g), NaCl (1.28 g), and NaNO3 (0.66 g).
Top off to the 20 L fill line and mix with a sterile instrument.
Loosely seal with the lid and store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Establish Microbial Mats in Reactors
steps.instruction: Seed the reactors with field-derived benthic biomats.

substeps.instruction: Collect ~6.5 L of surficial benthic biomat using 1 L Nalgene bottles; transport at 4 °C.
Clean reactors with a dilute bleach soak, water rinse, 70% ethanol wipe, and air dry.
Mark the interior of reactors with 25 mm vertical increments or use rulers.
Homogenize field sample using autoclaved utensils and add to reactors to a target depth of ~1 cm (or 2 cm for validation).
Add influent media to desired depth (e.g., 3.5 cm water column) and let settle for ~12 h with lights off.
Start influent flow to achieve a hydraulic residence time in the open water column of 12–48 h.
Optional: Operate a parallel biomat-free reactor as a control.

steps.title: Operate Diel Cycling
steps.instruction: Manage light and flow to simulate natural conditions.

substeps.instruction: Set light cycles (typically 12 h on / 12 h off) with one-hour light ramps to mimic sunrise/sunset.
Adjust light intensity (e.g., 5%, 15%, or 30% of max output) to tune pH and DO fluctuations.
Monitor pH and DO at 15 to 30-min intervals for multiple 24 h cycles until steady-state is observed (typically 5–7 days).
